messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want libraries in New York with Reading Room and Fiction; in Los Angeles with Wi-Fi and Children Section; in Chicago with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function signature expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

But the facilities parameter seems to accept a single value or an array? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." Then lists options separated by |. For "Cafe" it shows "Cafe"[], maybe meaning array of cafes? But likely we pass an array of strings? The type is ambiguous. We might pass an array of strings for multiple facilities. Let's assume we pass an array of strings for multiple facilities. So for NY: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]; LA: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]; Chicago: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We'll call the function three times.
